notes: The weapons effects' game values (docs/fx/README.md 4.1, 6), read by Unreal's USimFxSubsystem (unreal/SAM3D/Source/SAM3D/Private/SimFxTuning.cpp); a key left out keeps the code's default. Sizes in metres, times in seconds, speeds in m/s, colours linear RGB. Brightness is in multiples of a white surface lit by the level's sun (ASimSkyWeatherActor's 10 lux; sam3d.fx.EmissiveScale scales it, and a brighter sun scales it with its lux). Explosion sizes themselves come from simcore (fx::LookFor: W^(1/3) scaling); these are the drawing's counts, colours and timings.

origins.trail_margin_m: sam3d game value: a trail is laid and drawn to the effects' range or the weather's visibility, whichever is nearer, plus this (docs/fx/README.md 4.1; a trail is long, and its near end may be in range while the point laid is a little past it)
origins.contrail_range_scale: sam3d game value: a contrail is laid out to twice the effects' range (sam3d.fx.MaxRange), the long white line seen far off in clear air (LOOK.md 12), but never past the visibility
origins.glint_sprite_px: LOOK.md 15 (under 6 px a burst is a glint, glint_px 3): a night point light's glow sprite 6 px wide, whose bright core (T_FX_Glow's middle third) is about the 3 px glint (at 8 px the saturated core measured 6-7 px across in art-polish-2's pictures); a sam3d game value
origins.glint_keep: sam3d game value: a night glint at its pixel floor keeps at least half its opacity, not its true area's share (a motor at 1.3-3 km and an afterburner at 2.4 km were one dim pixel or nothing: the coordinator's look of 1 Nov)
origins.speck_px: LOOK.md T12 and 3 (a 15 m puff at 5 km, 4.7 px, is shown as a grey speck by day); 1.5 px, the smallest a sprite is drawn, is a sam3d game value

origins.smoke_sun: sam3d game value: the sun's light on smoke and trails against a surface's, as a photograph exposed for the ground holds sunlit smoke short of white: a puff's lit side about 1.4 x its albedo with smoke_sky (LOOK 9.3: lit #E7E6E3, undersides #A8A39A; LOOK 0.2: a column's top #8C8984; the second art review's item 1 measured them all 1.5-2 x too bright at 0.6 and the sky's whole light)
origins.smoke_sky: sam3d game value: the sky's light on smoke and trails, a share of what lights the ground's shade (with smoke_sun); 0.8 not 0.6 because at 0.6 a backlit column's top went to lum 86 against LOOK 0.2's #8C8984 (art-polish, the FAB-500 at 5 s)
origins.smoke_sky_low: sam3d game value: the sky's light on a puff's underside, which sees the ground, against its top (the second art review's item 1: undersides lit as fully as tops); 0.65 of the sky's light on an underside (0.55 left a backlit column's root lum 50-62 against LOOK 0.2's #4A4540, art-polish); with the sun's share an underside about 0.35-0.4 of a lit top's light, LOOK 9.3's #A8A39A against #E7E6E3
origins.ambient_night: LOOK.md 15 (smoke unseen at night unless a flash, a fire or the moon lights it): a full moon's 0.25 lux against a 100000-lux sun
origins.ambient_dusk: the sky's share is ambient_dusk to the sun 6 degrees under the horizon, then falls a decade every 2 degrees (nautical twilight, N1) to ambient_night
